ety.text: Inherited from Middle English table, tabel, tabil, tabul, from Old English tabele, tabul, tablu, tabule, tabula (“board”); also as tæfl, tæfel, an early Germanic borrowing of Latin tabula (“tablet, board, plank, chart”). The sense of “piece of furniture” is from Old French table, of same Latin origin; Old English used bēod or bord instead for this meaning: see board. Doublet of tabula and tavla.

senses.d: An item of furniture with a flat top surface raised above the ground, usually on one or more legs.
ex: Set that dish on the table over there, please.

senses.d: A flat tray which can be used as a table.
A supply of food or entertainment.
ex: The baron kept a fine table and often held large banquets.

senses.d: A booth or display at an event such as an exposition or fair.
A service of Holy Communion.
The board or table-like furniture on which a game is played, such as snooker, billiards, or draughts.
One half of a backgammon board, which is divided into an inner and outer table.
The game of backgammon, or any of several related games.
A group of people at a table, for example, for a meal, meeting or game; a meeting at a table.
The act of assembling to eat; a gathering to eat, especially at a restaurant.
ex: Time to come to table.
Join us at the table I booked at the restaurant.

senses.d: To tabulate; to put into a table or grid.
ex: to table fines

senses.d: To supply (a guest, client etc.) with food at a table; to feed.
ex:
'April 13 1638, Henry Wotton, letter to John Milton
At Siena I was tabled in the house of one Alberto Scipioni

senses.d: To delineate; to represent, as in a picture; to depict.
ex:
c. 1607, Francis Bacon, letter to Tobie Matthew
tabled and pictured in the chambers of meditation

senses.d: To put on the table of a commission or legislative assembly; to propose for formal discussion or consideration, to put on the agenda.
To remove from the agenda, to postpone dealing with; to shelve (to indefinitely postpone consideration or discussion of something).
ex: The legislature tabled the amendment, so they will not be discussing it until later.
The motion was tabled, ensuring that it would not be taken up until a later date.

senses.d: To represent a company or organization (at an exposition, fair, etc.), usually at a booth or display.
To join (pieces of timber) together using coaks.
To put on a table.
To show one's cards face-up, especially during showdown.
To make board hems in the skirts and bottoms of (sails) in order to strengthen them in the part attached to the bolt-rope.

senses.d: An inhibition or ban that results from social custom or emotional aversion.
ex: It is true indeed that a taboo - in order to be a proper taboo - must not rest in the general mind on argument or reason.

senses.d: Culturally forbidden.
